Definition: of Chaldee origin (H2); father as a vocative:--Abba.
BiblicalUsage: Abba is the Aramaic word for father, kept in its own language in the Greek New Testament — a child's word, intimate and direct. Jesus cries it in Gethsemane, 'Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee'; Paul says believers have received 'the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father'; and the Spirit of God's Son cries it in our hearts.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this is the tenderest word in the New Testament: the Son's own word for His Father, given to us. Because Christ prayed 'Abba' in the garden, I can pray it too — not as a slave begging a master, but as a child coming home to a Father who has already adopted me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
